no mls qos

stem: Why is voice normally kept in its own VLAN, separate from the data VLAN that serves the PCs?
explanation: A dedicated voice VLAN lets the network apply a QoS policy, a security policy, and a DHCP scope to phones alone, and it keeps PC broadcast traffic away from latency-sensitive call signalling. A phone sharing the data VLAN cannot be given different treatment without also treating the PCs that way.

choices.text: So QoS, security policy, and the DHCP scope can target phone traffic independently of PC traffic
Because a phone cannot tag frames unless it is in a separate VLAN
Because voice VLANs bypass spanning tree to reduce latency
Because trunking requires at least two VLANs on every port

stem: A switch receives a frame whose destination MAC address is not present in its MAC address table. What does it do with the frame?
explanation: An unknown destination cannot be mapped to a port, so the switch floods the frame out every other port in the same VLAN. That flooding is exactly what a MAC flooding attack exploits, filling the table with bogus entries so legitimate destinations also look unknown.

choices.text: Floods it out of every other port in the same VLAN
Drops it and sends an ICMP unreachable message
Sends it only to the default gateway port
Holds it until the destination sends a frame and is learned

stem: Which command lists the MAC addresses a switch has learned, along with their VLANs and ports?
explanation: show mac address-table prints the CAM contents with VLAN, type, and port so you can confirm whether a host was learned on the expected access port. It is the first check when a host is reachable from some parts of the network but not others.

choices.text: show mac address-table
show arp
show interface status
show vlan brief

stem: Which statement is true of a MAC address entry created with the mac address-table static command?
explanation: Static entries are administrative and are never aged out, unlike dynamically learned ones that disappear after the aging time or a reload. That permanence is useful for pinned server ports, but it also means a stale static entry survives until someone removes it.

choices.text: It is never aged out and remains until it is removed manually
It ages out after 300 seconds like a dynamic entry
It is cleared whenever the switch is reloaded
It can only be created on a trunk port

stem: A single MAC address keeps appearing on two different switch ports within seconds of each other. What does this most likely indicate?
explanation: The switch follows the source address of the newest frame, so the entry bounces between ports as frames arrive from both directions. That flapping is the classic signature of a Layer 2 loop, or of a duplicated MAC such as a cloned VM or a misconfigured NIC team.

choices.text: A Layer 2 loop or a duplicated MAC address
Normal ageing behaviour of dynamic entries
The switch running out of CAM table space
A mismatch between the native VLANs on a trunk

stem: Which command enables storm control for broadcast traffic at 20 percent of the interface bandwidth?
explanation: The level keyword takes a percentage of the interface's total bandwidth when no unit is given, and each traffic type is configured separately. Broadcast, multicast, and unknown unicast therefore need three separate statements if all three should be limited.

choices.text: storm-control broadcast level 20
storm-control broadcast 20 mbps
storm-control level broadcast 20
switchport storm-control broadcast 20

stem: Which storm-control action keyword takes the port out of service when the configured threshold is exceeded?
explanation: The shutdown keyword err-disables the interface, which stops the storm but also drops every legitimate frame on that port. The trap keyword only reports the condition, and plain storm control with no action simply discards the excess traffic while the port stays up.

choices.text: shutdown
trap
restrict
protect

stem: Storm control with the shutdown action placed a port in the err-disabled state. What restores it?
explanation: An err-disabled port has to be cycled with shutdown and no shutdown, or recovered automatically if errdisable recovery has been enabled for the storm-control cause. Either way the underlying storm has to be resolved first, or the port will simply be disabled again.

choices.text: Issue shutdown then no shutdown, or enable errdisable recovery for the storm-control cause
Clear the MAC address table
Reload the switch
Remove the storm-control command from the interface

stem: Which storm-control syntax limits broadcast traffic to a packet rate rather than a percentage of bandwidth?
explanation: Adding the pps keyword switches the threshold from a percentage of the interface bandwidth to packets per second, which is far more predictable on links whose speed is not fixed. A percentage on a 10 Gbps port allows an enormous packet rate that may still overwhelm a slow attached device.

choices.text: storm-control broadcast level pps 500
storm-control broadcast rate 500 pps
storm-control broadcast packets 500
storm-control broadcast level 500 bps

stem: What are the default CDP advertisement interval and hold time on a Cisco device?
explanation: CDP sends an advertisement every 60 seconds and tells the neighbour to keep the entry for 180 seconds, so three advertisements can be lost before the neighbour is removed. Both values can be changed with the cdp timer and cdp holdtime commands.

choices.text: 60 seconds interval, 180 seconds hold time
30 seconds interval, 120 seconds hold time
120 seconds interval, 360 seconds hold time
10 seconds interval, 30 seconds hold time

stem: Which interface command stops CDP from advertising on a single port while leaving CDP running globally?
explanation: no cdp enable disables CDP on that one interface, which is what a hardening baseline does on ports facing an untrusted network. The global no cdp run would disable the protocol everywhere and break neighbour discovery on every other link.

choices.text: no cdp enable
no cdp run
no cdp advertise-v2
cdp disable

stem: Which command shows a CDP neighbour's platform, software version, and management address rather than just its name and port?
explanation: show cdp neighbors prints one line per neighbour with the local port and the neighbour's port, while the detail keyword adds the platform, IOS version, and address list. Those extra fields are what let you verify a device's software release remotely.

choices.text: show cdp neighbors detail
show cdp neighbors
show cdp interface
show cdp traffic

stem: Which two interface commands control whether a port sends and accepts LLDP advertisements?
explanation: LLDP is enabled globally with lldp run and then tuned per interface with lldp transmit and lldp receive separately. That split is useful on an edge port where you want to receive neighbour data but not advertise the switch's own identity, or the reverse.

choices.text: lldp transmit and lldp receive
lldp run and no lldp run
lldp enable and lldp disable
lldp advertise and lldp listen

stem: What does 802.11r fast BSS transition change about a client roaming between access points?
explanation: A normal roam repeats the full authentication and key exchange at the new AP, which is slow enough to break a voice call. 802.11r pre-establishes the security keys across the mobility domain so the client can resume at the new AP with a short handshake instead of a full one.

choices.text: It pre-establishes keys so the client can rekey quickly at the new access point
It gives the client a list of neighbour access points to consider
It encrypts management frames to prevent deauthentication attacks
It lets the client keep its IP address across different subnets

stem: Several clients use an SSID successfully, but one laptop can see the SSID and still fails to join. What is the most likely cause?
explanation: An SSID that broadcasts correctly but rejects one specific client usually means a policy the client cannot satisfy, such as a WPA3-only WLAN when the adapter only supports WPA2, or a protected management frames requirement the driver does not implement. The radio link is working, so the failure happens at the security stage.

choices.text: The client does not support the security policy the WLAN requires, such as WPA3 or protected management frames
The SSID is hidden from that client only
The client is out of range of every access point
The DHCP scope for the WLAN is exhausted

stem: A wireless client joins the correct SSID and gets an address, but it lands in the wrong VLAN. Where is the mapping defined?
explanation: The controller decides which VLAN a wireless client belongs to by mapping the WLAN to an interface or VLAN, and the frame is then tagged onto the trunk toward the access switch. A client in the wrong subnet is therefore a mapping mistake on the controller, not a problem with the client or the AP.

choices.text: In the WLAN-to-interface mapping on the wireless controller
In the client's own IP configuration
In the access point's radio profile
In the DHCP scope on the client's subnet

stem: What does client exclusion do on a wireless controller?
explanation: Client exclusion blocks a specific MAC address for a configured period after repeated authentication or association failures. It limits the damage from a client stuck in a failing retry loop, but it also means a misconfigured device stays off the network even after the configuration is corrected until the timer expires.

choices.text: It blocks a client's MAC address for a period after repeated failures
It removes the client from the controller's mobility group
It permanently denies every client that misses a DHCP request
It disables the SSID the client was trying to join

stem: Which pair of commands defines a local SPAN session that copies traffic from Gi0/1 to Gi0/2?
explanation: A SPAN session always needs both a source and a destination statement under the same session number. The source can be an interface or a VLAN, and the destination is the port where the analyzer is plugged in.

choices.text: monitor session 1 source interface Gi0/1, then monitor session 1 destination interface Gi0/2
span source Gi0/1, then span destination Gi0/2
monitor capture Gi0/1 both, then monitor export Gi0/2
interface Gi0/1 monitor, then interface Gi0/2 mirror

stem: How does a port behave while it is the destination of a SPAN session?
explanation: A SPAN destination port gives up its normal switching role and transmits only the mirrored copies, so it neither forwards user traffic nor learns addresses. Attaching a device that answers on that port can disturb the capture, which is why analyzers usually just listen.

choices.text: It stops forwarding normal user traffic and only transmits the mirrored copies
It forwards user traffic and mirrored copies at the same time by default
It becomes a trunk carrying the mirrored VLAN
It shuts down until the session is removed

stem: What does a SPAN session capture when its source is configured as a VLAN instead of an interface?
explanation: A VLAN source mirrors traffic on every port that belongs to that VLAN, including frames switched between two local hosts that never leave the switch. That makes it useful for capturing a whole segment, at the cost of far more traffic than a single port would generate.

choices.text: Traffic on every port in that VLAN, including frames switched locally between hosts
Only traffic that leaves the switch toward the default gateway
Only broadcast and multicast frames in that VLAN
Only frames arriving on the trunk ports carrying that VLAN

stem: Which VLAN-level command must be applied to the VLAN that carries mirrored frames in an RSPAN session?
explanation: An RSPAN VLAN has to be declared with remote-span so the switches treat it as a transport for mirrored traffic rather than a normal VLAN. Without it the mirrored frames are flooded normally and the session never delivers a clean capture to the destination switch.

choices.text: remote-span, entered in VLAN configuration mode
monitor session 1 remote vlan
spanning-tree portfast, entered on every port in the VLAN
vlan dot1q tag native on each trunk

stem: Two virtual machines on the same hypervisor and the same port group exchange frames. Does that traffic reach the physical network?
explanation: The virtual switch forwards between vNICs in software, so the frames are delivered without ever touching an uplink. That is why a capture taken on the physical switch sees nothing for this traffic and the analyzer has to run inside the hypervisor instead.

choices.text: No; the virtual switch forwards the frames internally in software
Yes; every frame is sent to the physical switch first
Only if the two virtual machines are in different VLANs
Only if promiscuous mode is enabled on the port group

stem: What does NIC teaming provide when several physical adapters are attached to one virtual switch?
explanation: Teaming bonds multiple physical NICs into one logical uplink, so a failed adapter does not take the host off the network and the aggregate bandwidth exceeds that of a single link. The exact load-balancing behaviour depends on the policy chosen and on how the physical switch is configured.

choices.text: Redundancy if an adapter fails and more bandwidth than one link alone
A separate VLAN for each virtual machine automatically
Encryption of all traffic leaving the host
A guarantee that each virtual machine uses a dedicated physical NIC

stem: Which port group security policy stops a virtual machine from presenting a MAC address that was never assigned to it?
explanation: The MAC address changes policy governs frames received from the guest, and forged transmits covers frames the guest sends with a source MAC it does not own. Rejecting both closes the spoofing hole that otherwise lets one virtual machine impersonate another on the same segment.

choices.text: MAC address changes, together with forged transmits
Promiscuous mode
Traffic shaping
The uplink teaming policy

stem: How is a virtual machine's traffic placed into a specific VLAN on a standard virtual switch?
explanation: The port group carries the VLAN ID and the virtual switch tags frames as they leave toward the uplink, so the guest itself stays VLAN-unaware. The alternative is to give the guest a trunk and let it tag its own frames, which requires the port group to allow VLAN 4095.

choices.text: The port group holds the VLAN ID and the virtual switch tags the frames
The guest operating system must tag its own frames in every case
The physical switch detects the guest and assigns a VLAN dynamically
Each virtual machine is bound to a dedicated uplink in that VLAN

stem: Which legacy Cisco feature gives an access switch an immediate alternate path when its root port fails?
explanation: UplinkFast keeps a secondary uplink ready and moves it straight to forwarding when the root port goes down, instead of waiting through the 802.1D listening and learning timers. It also limits how much the switch can disturb the topology, which is why it is meant only for access-layer switches.

choices.text: UplinkFast
Root Guard
Loop Guard
BPDU Guard

stem: What does BPDU Filter do when it is applied to a PortFast interface?
explanation: BPDU Filter stops the port from sending BPDUs and ignores any it receives, which effectively removes the port from spanning tree. That is safe only toward an end host; accidentally applying it toward another switch creates exactly the loop spanning tree exists to prevent.

choices.text: It stops sending BPDUs and ignores received BPDUs, effectively removing the port from spanning tree
It places the port in the root-inconsistent state when a superior BPDU arrives
It converts the port into a designated port regardless of topology
It slows the port's transition to forwarding to detect loops

stem: Which command makes a switch automatically re-enable ports that BPDU Guard has err-disabled?
explanation: errdisable recovery cause bpduguard enables automatic recovery, and the interval is set separately, defaulting to 300 seconds. Without it, every BPDU Guard violation needs a manual shutdown and no shutdown on the port.

choices.text: errdisable recovery cause bpduguard
spanning-tree bpduguard enable recovery
no spanning-tree bpduguard default
errdisable detect cause bpduguard

stem: Which three port states exist in Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (802.1w)?
explanation: RSTP folded the 802.1D disabled, blocking, and listening states into a single discarding state, leaving discarding, learning, and forwarding. Fewer states mean a port can move directly from discarding to forwarding once the proposal and agreement exchange succeeds.

choices.text: Discarding, learning, and forwarding
Blocking, listening, and forwarding
Disabled, blocking, and learning
Discarding, listening, and forwarding

stem: How does an RSTP edge port behave when a cable is plugged into it?
explanation: An edge port assumes an end host is attached, so it moves straight to forwarding without the proposal and agreement exchange and without generating a topology change. It is the RSTP equivalent of PortFast, and the same caution applies: connecting another switch to it invites a loop.

choices.text: It moves directly to forwarding and does not trigger a topology change
It waits for the proposal and agreement handshake before forwarding
It becomes the root port for the segment
It stays in discarding until a BPDU is received

stem: How quickly does RSTP conclude that a neighbour on a point-to-point link has failed?
explanation: RSTP treats the loss of three consecutive hellos as a failure, which at the default two-second hello interval is about six seconds. That is far faster than 802.1D, which waits out the full max-age timer before even beginning to reconverge.

choices.text: After three missed hellos, roughly six seconds at the default interval
After the 20-second max-age timer expires
After 30 seconds of listening and learning
Only when the interface line protocol goes down

stem: Which interface command disables Power over Ethernet delivery on a switch port?
explanation: power inline never stops the port from detecting and powering a device, which is what you want on a port that should only ever serve a non-PoE host. It is a per-port setting, so the rest of the switch keeps powering phones and access points normally.

choices.text: power inline never
no power inline
power inline off
poe disable

stem: Which mechanism does 802.3at use beyond hardware classification to negotiate power above the 15.4 W class limit?
explanation: Hardware classification only carries a few power classes, so 802.3at adds LLDP-based negotiation that lets the powered device and the PSE agree on a higher figure. That is how a PoE+ access point can request 25 W rather than being capped at the class ceiling.

choices.text: LLDP power negotiation between the powered device and the PSE
A second round of resistance detection at a higher voltage
CDP advertisements carrying a wattage field
DHCP option 82 in the device's address request

stem: A powered device draws more current than the PSE allocated to its port. What does the PSE do?
explanation: The PSE monitors the port and removes power when the device exceeds its allocation, which protects the switch's power supply and the cabling. The port then has to go through detection again before power is restored, so an undersized allocation looks like a device that keeps rebooting.

choices.text: It removes power from the port and the device must be detected again
It delivers the extra power and logs a warning
It drops the port's data traffic but keeps power applied
It moves the device to a higher power class automatically

stem: What is the default port security violation mode on a Cisco switch?
explanation: The default is shutdown, which err-disables the port on the first violation and raises a syslog message. Because that takes the port out of service, many access designs deliberately change it to restrict so a single unauthorised device does not silence a working port.

choices.text: shutdown
restrict
protect
trap

stem: Which links carry VTP advertisements between switches?
explanation: VTP advertisements are sent only over trunk links, so a switch reachable solely through access ports never learns the domain's VLAN database. That is why a new switch cabled to an access port can sit in the domain with a stale database and no error.

choices.text: Trunk links only
Any link between two switches, access or trunk
Only links configured as EtherChannel members
Only routed links between Layer 3 switches

stem: A phone on a Cisco access port cannot be told the voice VLAN ID, but its 802.1p priority marking must survive. Which voice VLAN option does that?
explanation: The dot1p option is for phones that mark priority but not a VLAN: voice frames arrive in a priority tag whose VLAN ID is zero, and the switch reads the CoS bits and places them into the configured voice VLAN. Marking survives even though the phone never learns the VLAN number.

choices.text: switchport voice vlan dot1p
switchport voice vlan untagged
switchport voice vlan none
switchport voice vlan priority

stem: How does port security violation mode `protect` differ from `restrict`?
explanation: Protect is the quiet mode: frames from unauthorized addresses are dropped exactly as with restrict, but no syslog message, SNMP trap, or violation counter is produced, so a flood of violations cannot fill the log. Restrict offers the same drop behaviour with visibility; shutdown takes the port down instead.

choices.text: It drops frames from violating addresses but produces no log, trap, or counter increment
It shuts the port down and requires manual recovery
It forwards the violating frames but flags the port as err-disabled
It disables port security on that port until the next reload

stem: In the output of `show storm-control`, what does the Filter State column report?
explanation: The level columns show the configured rising and falling thresholds; Filter State says what the switch is doing right now, Forwarding below the threshold and Blocking once the rising threshold is crossed. A port sitting in Blocking with modest levels usually points at a loop or one very chatty host.

choices.text: Whether traffic of that type is currently forwarded or blocked because the threshold is exceeded
How many frames have been dropped since the counters were cleared
Whether the interface is configured with the shutdown action
The remaining errdisable recovery time for the port

stem: Why does a switch keep a separate MAC address table entry scope for each VLAN instead of one global table?
explanation: The table is keyed by VLAN as well as by MAC, so two isolated VLANs can each hold the same address on different ports without colliding. That is also why `show mac address-table vlan <id>` is the useful query when the ports look right but traffic still floods.

choices.text: Because the same MAC address can legitimately appear in more than one VLAN, so entries are scoped to the VLAN
Because VLAN tags are longer than MAC addresses and need their own index
Because each trunk needs a separate copy of the table per tag
Because the VLAN is only determined after the destination has been resolved

stem: What is the effect of the global configuration command `no cdp run` on a switch?
explanation: `no cdp run` stops the CDP process device-wide, so per-interface `cdp enable` is moot until the process is restarted with `cdp run`. The per-port alternative, `no cdp enable`, silences one interface while the rest of the switch keeps advertising.

choices.text: CDP stops on every interface, including those still configured with cdp enable
CDP stops only on interfaces that lack an explicit cdp enable
CDP keeps running but only listens, no longer advertising
CDP stops on trunk ports while access ports keep advertising

stem: On a segment between two non-root switches, one port becomes a root port and the other becomes a designated port. What decides which port is designated?
explanation: The port on the switch with the lowest cumulative path cost to the root bridge wins the segment and becomes designated. The losing switch keeps a root port facing the winner.

choices.text: The port on the switch with the lower cumulative path cost to the root bridge becomes designated
The port with the lower port number on the higher-priority switch becomes designated
The port on the switch with the higher bridge priority becomes designated
The port that receives the first BPDU after the topology changes becomes designated

stem: How does RSTP converge a point-to-point link without waiting for the forward-delay timers?
explanation: RSTP uses a proposal and agreement handshake. The downstream switch synchronises its other ports and answers with an agreement, so the link moves to forwarding immediately instead of waiting through listening and learning.

choices.text: The downstream switch synchronises its ports and replies to a proposal with an agreement
It floods a topology change notification and waits for the forward-delay timer to expire
It relies on the root bridge to resend configuration BPDUs every two seconds
It disables the link and re-enables it once the max-age timer expires

stem: How many links can be active in one standard LACP EtherChannel bundle, and what happens to additional compatible links?
explanation: LACP supports a maximum of eight active links in a bundle. Up to eight more compatible links can be placed in hot-standby and take over if an active member fails.

choices.text: Eight links are active and up to eight more can sit in hot standby
Sixteen links are active and none can be held in standby
Four links are active and the remainder are placed in err-disabled state
Two links are active and the remainder are blocked by spanning tree

stem: An EtherChannel is configured on one switch only, while the neighbouring switch still treats all four links as separate. What is the result?
explanation: A bundle needs matching configuration on both ends. With only one side bundled the channel does not form, so the four parallel links look like a loop and spanning tree blocks three of them.

choices.text: The channel does not form, and spanning tree blocks three of the four links
The channel forms with one quarter of the expected bandwidth
The channel forms but only one member link passes traffic
All four links forward at once and create a broadcast storm

stem: A trunk port's allowed VLAN list contains only VLANs 10 and 20. A frame tagged for VLAN 30 arrives on that port. What does the switch do with it?
explanation: The allowed VLAN list is an ingress and egress filter. A tagged frame for a VLAN that is not permitted on the trunk is discarded rather than mapped or flooded.

choices.text: It drops the frame
It forwards the frame into the native VLAN
It adds VLAN 30 to the allowed list automatically
It floods the frame to every port in VLAN 30

stem: What does VTP pruning accomplish in a switched network?
explanation: Pruning stops a VLAN's flooded traffic from crossing trunk links that have no active ports in that VLAN, which saves bandwidth on trunks that do not need the broadcast domain.

choices.text: It stops flooding for a VLAN on trunk links that have no active ports in that VLAN
It removes unused VLANs from the VLAN database automatically
It compresses VTP advertisements between switches
It deletes stale MAC address entries from the CAM table

stem: An 802.3af port allocates 15.4 W at the PSE, yet the standard guarantees only 12.95 W at the powered device. What accounts for the difference?
explanation: The 2.45 W gap covers resistive loss in the cable plant over the full 100-meter channel. The PSE must budget for that loss so the device still receives its guaranteed class power.

choices.text: Power dissipated in the cable plant over a 100-meter run
Power the powered device must reserve for PoE passthrough
A reserve held back for LLDP power negotiation
Derating applied by the PSE when shielded cable is detected

stem: A multilayer switch receives a frame addressed to its own VLAN 10 SVI MAC address, and the encapsulated packet is destined for a host in VLAN 20. What does the switch do?
explanation: A frame addressed to the SVI MAC is destined for the switch itself, so the switch routes it: it strips the Layer 2 header, decrements the TTL, looks up the VLAN 20 destination, and rewrites the frame for that VLAN.

choices.text: It strips the Layer 2 header, rewrites it for VLAN 20, decrements the TTL, and forwards
It floods the frame to every access port in VLAN 20
It drops the frame because SVIs cannot route between VLANs
It sends the frame back out VLAN 10 toward the default gateway

stem: A switch has a dynamic MAC table entry binding 00:1a:2b:3c:4d:5e to Gi0/4. A frame with that source MAC then arrives on Gi0/9. What does the switch do?
explanation: Source addresses are learned on ingress. Seeing the same MAC on a new port means the station moved, so the switch overwrites the existing entry and points it at Gi0/9.

choices.text: It updates the entry so the MAC now points at Gi0/9
It drops the frame as a spoofing attempt
It logs a port security violation and err-disables Gi0/9
It keeps both entries and load-balances between them

stem: In the command `monitor session 1 source interface Gi0/1 both`, what does the `both` keyword include in the capture?
explanation: The direction keyword selects ingress, egress, or both. `both` mirrors frames received on the interface and frames transmitted from it.

choices.text: Frames received on and frames transmitted from Gi0/1
Both unicast and multicast frames
Both IPv4 and IPv6 frames
Both tagged and untagged frames

stem: Two virtual machines run on the same hypervisor but in port groups mapped to VLAN 10 and VLAN 20. How can they exchange traffic?
explanation: A virtual switch preserves VLAN separation the same way a physical switch does. Frames cannot cross between VLAN 10 and VLAN 20 inside the host, so the traffic must be routed by a Layer 3 device.

choices.text: Only through a Layer 3 device, because the virtual switch keeps the VLANs separate
Directly, because a virtual switch ignores VLAN IDs for traffic that stays local
Only after promiscuous mode is enabled on both port groups
Only after NIC teaming is configured on the uplink

stem: Port security is configured with `switchport port-security mac-address sticky` and the switch is then reloaded. What happens to the learned secure addresses?
explanation: Sticky learning writes the addresses into the running configuration, not into NVRAM by itself. Unless the configuration was saved before the reload, the addresses are lost and relearned.

choices.text: They survive only if the running configuration was saved before the reload
They always survive because sticky entries are written directly to NVRAM
They are always lost because sticky entries exist only in RAM and never reach the configuration
They are converted into static entries automatically during the reload

stem: A switch looks up the destination MAC of an incoming frame and finds it mapped to the very port the frame arrived on. What does the switch do?
explanation: If the destination is reached through the ingress port, the destination is on the same segment as the sender and needs no forwarding. The switch filters, meaning it drops the frame.

choices.text: It filters the frame and sends nothing
It floods the frame to all other ports in the VLAN
It forwards the frame back out the ingress port
It clears the entry and then floods the frame

stem: A switch port is configured `switchport mode dynamic auto`. What must the neighbour do for the link to become a trunk?
explanation: Dynamic auto waits passively. It only forms a trunk when the far end actively asks for one, meaning the neighbour must be in dynamic desirable or hard-coded trunk mode.

choices.text: Actively request trunking, as dynamic desirable or hard-coded trunk mode does
Also sit in dynamic auto, because two passive ends agree to trunk
Send VTP advertisements for the native VLAN
Be configured as an access port in the same VLAN

stem: How does Root Guard differ from BPDU Guard?
explanation: BPDU Guard err-disables a port the moment any BPDU arrives, because that port should never face a switch. Root Guard only reacts to a superior BPDU, placing the port in root-inconsistent state until the offending BPDUs stop.

choices.text: Root Guard reacts only to superior BPDUs and blocks the port temporarily, while BPDU Guard err-disables on any BPDU
Root Guard err-disables the port permanently, while BPDU Guard only logs the event
Root Guard applies to trunk ports and BPDU Guard applies to routed ports
They are the same feature under two names on different platforms

stem: Why is PortFast considered unsafe on a port that faces another switch?
explanation: PortFast skips listening and learning, so the port forwards immediately. Facing another switch, that instant forwarding can create a temporary loop before spanning tree converges.

choices.text: It forwards immediately and can create a temporary loop before spanning tree converges
It disables BPDU processing on the port entirely
It lowers the port's path cost and makes the switch root
It prevents the port from ever becoming a trunk

stem: What does the global command `spanning-tree portfast default` change?
explanation: It makes every access port on the switch run PortFast without per-interface configuration. Trunk ports are unaffected, and the setting still applies only to ports in access mode.

choices.text: Every access port runs PortFast without a per-interface command
Every port, trunk included, skips the listening and learning states
Spanning tree is disabled on all VLANs in the VLAN database
BPDU Guard is enabled on every access port automatically

stem: Which frame does a wireless client transmit first when looking for a known SSID?
explanation: A client that has a configured profile sends a directed probe request naming the SSID. Access points answer with probe responses, and the client then picks one to authenticate and associate with.

choices.text: A probe request naming the SSID
An association request
A four-way handshake message
A DHCP discover broadcast

stem: In the 802.11 join process, what is the correct order of the three management exchanges?
explanation: A client first authenticates with the AP under open-system or SAE authentication, then associates so the AP binds it to an SSID, and only after that does the data-confidentiality handshake run.

choices.text: Authentication, association, then the key-exchange handshake
Association, authentication, then the key-exchange handshake
Key-exchange handshake, authentication, then association
Authentication, key-exchange handshake, then association

stem: Which command shows LLDP neighbour details such as system description, capabilities, and management address?
explanation: `show lldp neighbors` gives a one-line summary per neighbour. The `detail` keyword adds the advertised system description, enabled capabilities, and management address.

choices.text: show lldp neighbors detail
show lldp interface
show lldp traffic
show cdp neighbors detail

stem: What are the default LLDP advertisement timer and hold time on a Cisco device?
explanation: LLDP sends an advertisement every 30 seconds and tells neighbours to keep it for 120 seconds, four times the interval. That ratio tolerates three lost advertisements before the entry ages out.

choices.text: 30 seconds and 120 seconds
60 seconds and 180 seconds
30 seconds and 90 seconds
5 seconds and 15 seconds

stem: Which command resets the interface error counters on a switch?
explanation: `clear counters` zeroes the counters on all interfaces, or on the one named in the command. Clearing them is the usual first step so that fresh errors can be attributed to a specific change.

choices.text: clear counters
reset interface counters
no interface counters
clear interface statistics all

stem: A switch port reports a growing count of late collisions. What does that indicate?
explanation: A late collision is detected after the first 64 bytes of a frame, which should be impossible in a healthy collision domain. It points to a duplex mismatch or a segment longer than the standard allows.

choices.text: A duplex mismatch or a cable run beyond the standard length
The interface is receiving frames tagged for an unallowed VLAN
The port is err-disabled by port security
The switch is dropping frames because the MAC table is full

stem: Which interface counter increments when a received frame is larger than the interface MTU allows?
explanation: Oversized frames are counted as giants. They usually mean a mismatch between the MTU configured on the two ends, or a jumbo-frame sender talking to a port left at the default.

choices.text: Giants
Runts
CRC errors
Input discards

stem: In `show interfaces status`, what does a port state of `notconnect` mean?
explanation: `notconnect` means the port has no link, so nothing is detected on the wire. It is distinct from `err-disabled`, where the port is shut down by a protection feature, and from `connected`, where link is up.

choices.text: The port has no link partner detected on the wire
The port is administratively shut down
The port was shut down by a protection feature
The port is up but has not learned any MAC addresses

stem: Why can storm control discard traffic that is not actually a storm?
explanation: Storm control counts all traffic of the selected type on the port, so a legitimate high rate of broadcast or multicast, such as video delivery, can cross the threshold and be treated like a flood.

choices.text: A legitimate high rate of broadcast or multicast traffic can cross the same threshold
Storm control cannot distinguish tagged from untagged frames
Storm control only counts frames sourced from the switch itself
The threshold is measured against CPU load rather than link rate

stem: Why is a storm-control threshold expressed as a percentage measured against interface bandwidth instead of a fixed rate?
explanation: A percentage scales with the link, so one policy works on a 1 Gbps access port and a 10 Gbps uplink. A fixed rate would mean something different on every speed and would need re-tuning per port.

choices.text: The same policy then scales automatically across ports of different speeds
Percentages are the only unit the hardware counters can report
A fixed rate cannot be configured on trunk ports
Percentages ignore the configured duplex setting, which fixed rates do not

stem: Which LLDP-MED type-length-value carries the voice VLAN identifier to an IP phone?
explanation: The network policy TLV tells the phone which VLAN ID, 802.1p priority, and DSCP value to use for voice. The phone applies those settings and starts tagging its own frames.

choices.text: The network policy TLV
The power via MDI TLV
The inventory management TLV
The location identification TLV

stem: Two Cisco switches are both set to dynamic desirable, yet the link stays an access port. Which mismatch would explain that?
explanation: DTP can agree on trunking, but the trunk still needs a common encapsulation. A mismatch between 802.1Q on one side and ISL on the other leaves the link unable to form a trunk.

choices.text: The two ends are configured with different trunk encapsulations
The two ends have different VTP revision numbers
The two ends are running different spanning-tree modes
The two ends have different native VLANs

stem: In the command `monitor session 1 source interface Gi0/1 rx`, what traffic is copied to the destination port?
explanation: The rx keyword restricts the capture to ingress frames, while tx captures egress and both captures the full bidirectional flow. Narrowing the direction halves the mirror volume.

choices.text: Only frames received on Gi0/1
Only frames transmitted from Gi0/1
Both received and transmitted frames on Gi0/1
All frames in the VLAN that Gi0/1 belongs to

stem: Why would an engineer attach an ACL to a SPAN session?
explanation: A filter ACL limits which frames are copied, which keeps a busy source from overrunning a slower destination port. It filters the copy, never the original traffic.

choices.text: To capture only the traffic of interest instead of every frame on the source
To block the mirrored traffic from reaching the destination port
To encrypt mirrored frames in transit
To raise the destination port's usable bandwidth

stem: How many wire pairs does 802.3af Power over Ethernet use to deliver power?
explanation: 802.3af and 802.3at push power over two pairs, using either the spare pairs or the data pairs depending on the implementation. Four-pair delivery only arrives with 802.3bt.

choices.text: Two pairs
All four pairs
One pair
Three pairs

stem: Why does a PSE run a detection step before applying power to a port?
explanation: Detection applies a low voltage and looks for the characteristic signature resistor of a powered device. Without a match the port stays unpowered, which protects ordinary Ethernet NICs.

choices.text: To confirm a valid powered device signature so non-PoE equipment is not damaged
To measure the cable length for billing purposes
To negotiate the Ethernet speed with the attached device
To check whether the device supports LLDP

stem: What distinguishes an RSTP alternate port from a backup port?
explanation: Both roles discard, but they differ in what they protect: an alternate port is a standby route to the root bridge, and a backup port is a standby route to a segment the local switch already reaches.

choices.text: An alternate port offers another path toward the root, while a backup port offers a redundant path to the same shared segment
An alternate port is always forwarding, while a backup port always discards
An alternate port connects to a host, while a backup port connects to a switch
An alternate port exists only on the root bridge

stem: How does RSTP limit the impact of a topology change compared with 802.1D?
explanation: RSTP propagates a topology change notification hop by hop and flushes only the CAM entries on the affected links. 802.1D instead ages out addresses across the entire VLAN.

choices.text: It flushes only the ports affected by the change instead of the whole topology
It disables MAC learning for the whole VLAN during convergence
It waits for the maximum aging timer before forwarding again
It restarts the root election on every bridge

stem: Which three modes can a switch run under VTP version 2?
explanation: VTPv2 defines server, client, and transparent modes, and later platforms add an off mode. The root, designated, and alternate set belongs to spanning tree, not VTP.

choices.text: Server, client, and transparent
Primary, secondary, and standby
Master, slave, and monitor
Root, designated, and alternate

stem: Which capability does VTP version 3 add that version 2 lacks?
explanation: VTPv3 introduces the primary server concept, so only one switch is authoritative and every other server is a secondary that cannot change the database. It also adds per-VLAN control, extended VLAN support, and stronger authentication.

choices.text: A single primary server that must be designated before VLAN changes are accepted
Support for transparent mode
Propagation of VLAN additions across trunk links
A configuration revision number for advertisement comparison

stem: What does a VLAN trunking port group on a hypervisor virtual switch allow a guest to do?
explanation: A trunking port group passes 802.1Q tags through to the uplink instead of imposing one access VLAN. That lets a virtual firewall or router own several VLANs on a single vNIC.

choices.text: Tag its own frames with multiple VLAN IDs and have those tags carried to the physical switch
Bypass the physical switch entirely for inter-VLAN traffic
Assign itself any MAC address it chooses
Share a single VLAN with every other guest on the host

stem: Why is a separate management network recommended for hypervisor hosts?
explanation: Management interfaces control the host itself, so isolating them limits what an attacker sitting on a guest network can reach. It also keeps management traffic from competing with production workloads.

choices.text: It keeps hypervisor control traffic off guest VLANs so a compromised VM cannot reach the management plane
It doubles the available bandwidth for virtual machines
It removes the need for a physical switch uplink
It allows guests to share the host's IP address

stem: A multilayer switch routes a packet between two VLANs. What happens to the packet's IP TTL?
explanation: Routing a packet is a Layer 3 hop whether the device is called a router or a multilayer switch, so TTL is decremented and the header checksum recalculated. Hardware forwarding changes the speed, not the semantics.

choices.text: It is decremented by one as on any routed hop
It is reset to 255
It is left unchanged because the switch forwards in hardware
It is copied into the new Layer 2 header

stem: Which command removes dynamically learned MAC address entries from a switch's table?
explanation: The clear command with the dynamic keyword flushes learned entries and leaves static ones in place. A reload also clears dynamic entries because the table lives in RAM.

choices.text: clear mac address-table dynamic
no mac address-table
delete mac address-table
reset mac address-table

stem: Why does a switch age out dynamically learned MAC address entries?
explanation: Aging keeps the forwarding table consistent with where stations actually are. Without it, a device that moved would keep receiving traffic on its old port until the entry was overwritten.

choices.text: To drop entries for stations that have moved or gone away so stale ports are not used
To free space in the VLAN database
To force a new spanning-tree election
To keep the ARP cache synchronized

stem: What is a likely effect of setting the MAC address-table aging time very low on a busy access switch?
explanation: Entries expire before hosts stop sending, so frames for active destinations arrive with no matching table entry. The switch floods those unknown-unicast frames out every port in the VLAN, raising unnecessary traffic and CPU load.

choices.text: More frames are flooded as unknown unicast
The switch stops learning MAC addresses entirely
VLAN traffic is dropped at the trunk
The CPU disables cut-through forwarding

stem: Which forwarding method makes a switch verify a frame's FCS before forwarding it?
explanation: Store-and-forward receives the whole frame, checks the frame check sequence, and discards corrupt frames before forwarding. Cut-through begins forwarding after reading the destination MAC, which lowers latency but propagates errors.

choices.text: Store-and-forward
Cut-through
Fragment-free
Fast-forward

stem: Which VLAN is the native VLAN on an 802.1Q trunk by default?
explanation: Cisco switches use VLAN 1 as the native VLAN unless it is changed. Frames in the native VLAN cross the trunk untagged, which is why best practice is to move the native VLAN to an unused ID on both ends.

choices.text: VLAN 1
VLAN 0
VLAN 1005
VLAN 4095

stem: Why can VLANs 1002 through 1005 not be used for user traffic on a Cisco switch?
explanation: These IDs are reserved by default for legacy FDDI and Token Ring media translations. They appear in the VLAN database but cannot be assigned to access ports or deleted in normal operation.

choices.text: They are reserved for legacy media translations and cannot be assigned
They exceed the 802.1Q tag range
They are reserved for voice traffic only
They are used internally by VTP version 3

stem: A switch port is configured with an access VLAN for a workstation and a voice VLAN for an IP phone. How does the port handle the two traffic types?
explanation: The phone's own voice frames are tagged with the voice VLAN ID, while frames from the attached PC pass through the phone untagged and land in the access VLAN. This lets one port serve both devices without a second cable.

choices.text: Voice frames are tagged; PC frames are untagged in the access VLAN
Both traffic types are untagged in the voice VLAN
PC frames are tagged with the voice VLAN and voice frames are untagged
The port becomes a trunk and drops untagged frames

stem: Which DSCP value corresponds to the Expedited Forwarding per-hop behaviour used to mark voice payload?
explanation: Expedited Forwarding is DSCP 46, written as EF. It maps to the highest-priority queue in most QoS designs, giving voice a low-latency, low-jitter path ahead of data traffic.

stem: Which command limits a switch port to three learned MAC addresses?
explanation: The maximum parameter sets how many secure MAC addresses the port may learn. Once the limit is reached, any additional source MAC triggers the configured violation action.

choices.text: switchport port-security maximum 3
switchport port-security limit 3
switchport port-security mac-address 3
switchport port-security aging 3

stem: Which field of the output from show port-security interface shows how many times the port security rules have been broken?
explanation: The Security Violation Count counter increments each time a frame violates the configured maximum, sticky, or static address rules. It is the quickest way to confirm that a port is actually reacting to an offending device.

choices.text: Security Violation Count
Port Status
Maximum MAC Addresses
Aging Time

stem: Which 802.11 management frame does an access point send to end a client association without implying a security failure?
explanation: A disassociation frame ends an existing association, typically because the AP is rebooting, the client is idle, or the session is being torn down administratively. Deauthentication is a stronger statement that the client is no longer authenticated.

choices.text: Disassociation
Deauthentication
Probe response
Association request

stem: A wireless client is configured for 802.1X but the RADIUS server rejects its credentials. What is the visible result on the client?
explanation: The EAP exchange fails, so the authenticator never moves the port or the wireless session to the authorized state. The client cannot pass traffic even though it may still show the SSID as available or attempt to reconnect.

choices.text: Authentication fails and the client is never authorized to pass traffic
The client falls back to open authentication automatically
The AP assigns a static IP address instead
The client is placed in the voice VLAN

stem: Which information does LLDP-MED add beyond basic LLDP for voice endpoints?
explanation: LLDP-MED defines extensions such as network policy, power over MDI, inventory, and location identification. Network policy is what lets a phone learn its voice VLAN and QoS markings automatically.

choices.text: Network policy, power via MDI, inventory, and location TLVs
A routing table summary for the local subnet
Encrypted CAPWAP tunnel parameters
Spanning-tree topology change notifications

stem: Why should CDP be disabled on ports facing untrusted networks?
explanation: CDP advertisements expose the device model, software version, platform, and management addresses to anyone who can capture them. That information helps an attacker pick exploits and map the topology, so it is suppressed where the neighbour is not trusted.

choices.text: It reveals device model, software version, and management addresses
It consumes enough bandwidth to disrupt voice calls
It prevents STP from converging
It blocks DHCP snooping from binding addresses

stem: An EtherChannel is working, then one member interface is changed to a different speed. What happens to the bundle?
explanation: All members of a bundle must share speed, duplex, and VLAN parameters. A mismatch makes the offending interface incompatible, so it is suspended and removed from the channel, which can reduce total bandwidth or drop the channel if too few members remain.

choices.text: The mismatched interface is suspended and removed from the bundle
The bundle automatically negotiates a common speed
All members drop to half duplex
The channel converts to a routed port

stem: Why must the member interfaces of a Layer 2 EtherChannel be configured consistently before the bundle is relied on?
explanation: The switch validates that members agree on speed, duplex, allowed VLANs, and trunk state. Any disagreement causes the port to be suspended as a bundle mismatch, so the channel silently loses capacity instead of forwarding.

choices.text: Mismatched parameters cause member ports to suspend as bundle inconsistencies
The switch rewrites the configuration of the first member onto the others
STP disables the channel if any member differs
VTP refuses to advertise the VLAN database

stem: Place the 802.1D port states in the order a blocked port passes through them before it forwards traffic.
explanation: A port leaving the blocked state enters listening while it participates in the election, then learning while it populates the MAC table, and only then forwarding. Each transition waits for the forward delay timer, which is why convergence is slow without RSTP.

choices.text: Blocking, listening, learning, forwarding
Blocking, learning, listening, forwarding

Learning, blocking, listening, forwarding

stem: A storm-control threshold is configured as a percentage of link bandwidth. What happens to the effective threshold if the interface speed is increased?
explanation: The percentage is recalculated against the new link rate, so the same percentage permits a much higher absolute packet or bit rate. A threshold tuned on a 1 Gbps link can allow ten times the traffic after an upgrade to 10 Gbps.

choices.text: The permitted absolute rate rises with the new link speed
The threshold stays fixed in packets per second
Storm control is disabled automatically
The threshold halves to preserve the same absolute rate

stem: What is the default VTP operating mode on a Cisco switch?
explanation: A switch with no explicit VTP configuration runs in server mode. That is why a new switch with the null domain can join an existing domain and receive the VLAN database, which is also why a stray server can overwrite VLANs across the domain.

choices.text: Server
Client
Transparent
Off

stem: Two switches are connected by a trunk and both run VTP server mode, but their VTP domain names differ. What happens?
explanation: VTP updates are only accepted from neighbours in the same domain name, so with mismatched names the two databases stay independent. Each switch keeps its own VLAN list and neither synchronises, even though the trunk itself passes traffic normally.

choices.text: Each switch keeps its own VLAN database and no updates are exchanged
The switch with the higher revision number overwrites the other
The domain name is negotiated and both adopt the lower value
The trunk fails because VTP domain mismatch blocks 802.1Q

stem: Which two pieces of information does a DTP frame carry that let neighbours decide whether to form a trunk?
explanation: DTP advertises the sender VTP domain name and the desired trunk status, along with the neighbour identity and a timestamp. The domain field keeps unrelated switches from negotiating with each other, and the status field drives the auto and desirable state machine.

choices.text: The VTP domain name and the desired trunk status
The native VLAN and the allowed VLAN list
The spanning-tree priority and the bridge ID
The port speed and the duplex setting

stem: A port is left in DTP dynamic auto mode. How does it behave?
explanation: Dynamic auto waits passively: it will answer a trunk request from a desirable neighbour but never starts the negotiation itself. Two dynamic auto ports therefore settle as access ports, which is the usual cause of a trunk that will not come up.

choices.text: It responds to trunk requests but never initiates negotiation
It initiates negotiation every 30 seconds until a trunk forms
It always becomes a trunk regardless of the neighbour
It disables DTP and stays a permanent access port

stem: How does a multilayer switch derive the MAC address it uses for its switched virtual interfaces?
explanation: All SVIs share the switch chassis base MAC burned into the backplane; the SVI does not get a per-interface address. Because every SVI presents the same MAC, a host that moves between VLANs on the same switch still sees one consistent gateway MAC.

choices.text: It reuses the chassis base MAC for every SVI
It allocates a random MAC per VLAN at boot
It inherits the MAC of the first port in the VLAN
It queries a pool of MAC addresses from the supervisor

stem: A switch rejects the command `interface vlan 20` with an address that belongs to the same subnet as VLAN 10. Why?
explanation: The configuration is refused because two SVIs cannot hold addresses in the same subnet; each VLAN interface must own a distinct connected network. Overlapping subnets would make the CEF table ambiguous about which interface reaches a destination.

choices.text: Two VLAN interfaces cannot have addresses in the same subnet
VLAN 20 must be created before an SVI can be configured
The address is in the reserved 10.0.0.0/8 range
The switch only supports one SVI at a time

stem: A host on VLAN 30 must send a packet to a destination in VLAN 40 on the same multilayer switch. What MAC address does the host place in the frame?
explanation: The host compares the destination with its own subnet mask, sees a different network, and ARPs for its default gateway. The reply carries the SVI MAC, so the frame is addressed to the switch, which rewrites the Layer 2 header before forwarding into VLAN 40.

choices.text: The MAC of its default gateway SVI
The MAC of the destination host in VLAN 40
The broadcast address FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF
The chassis base MAC of the destination switch

stem: A switch without PoE support must power an 802.3af access point. What device solves this?
explanation: A midspan injector sits on the cable between the switch and the powered device and adds power to the spare pairs or through the data pairs. The switch keeps sending ordinary Ethernet while the injector supplies the 48 V, so no switch replacement is needed.

choices.text: A midspan power injector placed between the switch and the device
A crossover cable wired to pass power
A PoE splitter at the switch end of the cable
An inline UPS on the switch uplink

stem: Why do standards limit the power delivered per port when many PoE cables are bundled together?
explanation: Bundled cables trap heat, and the resulting temperature rise increases conductor resistance beyond what a single free-air cable would see. The bundle derating rules reduce the permitted current per pair so the insulation temperature rating is not exceeded.

choices.text: Trapped heat in the bundle raises conductor temperature and requires derating
The switch power supply cannot deliver power to adjacent ports
Bundled cables couple data signals and cause CRC errors
PoE detection fails when cables touch each other

stem: Two virtual machines on different ESXi hosts are configured with the same port group name and VLAN. How does their traffic reach each other?
explanation: The virtual switch is local to each host, so the frame leaves through the host physical NIC and crosses the physical network. It arrives on the other host and is delivered by that host virtual switch to the destination VM; the shared port group name only keeps the VLAN and policy consistent.

choices.text: It leaves the host NIC and crosses the physical network to the other host
It stays inside the local virtual switch of the first host
It is forwarded by the hypervisor kernel over a shared memory channel
It is dropped because port groups are host-local

stem: Why is the MTU on the physical NIC and the virtual switch raised when VXLAN is used?
explanation: VXLAN adds roughly 50 bytes of outer headers to each frame, so a 1500-byte guest frame becomes about 1550 bytes on the wire. Raising the underlay MTU, commonly to 1600, prevents fragmentation or drops for full-size guest traffic.

choices.text: VXLAN encapsulation adds about 50 bytes, so full-size frames need more MTU
VXLAN compresses frames and needs extra headroom for expansion
The virtual switch adds a checksum trailer to every frame
The physical NIC requires an MTU above 1500 to enable VLAN tagging

stem: How does Rapid PVST+ organise its spanning-tree instances?
explanation: Rapid PVST+ runs one 802.1w instance per VLAN, so each VLAN has its own root and its own blocking ports. That allows a different uplink to be active for each VLAN and gives sub-second convergence independently per VLAN.

choices.text: One instance per VLAN, each with its own root bridge
One instance for all VLANs sharing a single root
One instance per physical switch port
One instance per MST region mapped to all VLANs

stem: Which spanning-tree mode is the default on current Cisco IOS switches?
explanation: The default mode is Rapid PVST+ on modern Catalyst platforms. Sending `spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst` is normally redundant, though it is still common in configuration templates and exam answers.

choices.text: Rapid PVST+
PVST+
MST

stem: What VLAN range is allowed on an 802.1Q trunk by default?
explanation: A trunk allows VLANs 1 through 4094 by default, including the reserved and unused IDs in that span. The allowed list can be pruned with `switchport trunk allowed vlan`, but nothing is pruned until that command is issued.

choices.text: 1 through 4094
1 through 1005
1 through 1001
2 through 4094

stem: Which command output confirms that a VLAN is allowed on a trunk and forwarding in the spanning tree?
explanation: The `show interfaces trunk` output lists the allowed VLANs per trunk and, separately, the VLANs that are active and forwarding in spanning tree. Intersecting those two lists is the quickest check that traffic for a VLAN will actually cross the link.

choices.text: show interfaces trunk
show vlan brief
show spanning-tree summary
show interfaces switchport

stem: What is the difference between `switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20` and `switchport trunk allowed vlan add 30`?
explanation: Without the add keyword the command replaces the entire allowed list with the VLANs named. With add it appends to whatever is already permitted, which is why mixing the two forms out of order silently prunes VLANs.

choices.text: The first replaces the allowed list, the second appends to it
The first appends, the second replaces the allowed list

stem: A port mirror session copies traffic from a user port to an analyser. What happens to the original frames?
explanation: SPAN produces a copy while the switch continues to forward the original frame normally to its real destination. Mirroring is passive: it does not redirect, delay beyond normal switching, or alter the original frame in any way.

choices.text: They are still forwarded normally to their real destination
They are dropped after the copy is taken
They are tagged with the mirror VLAN before forwarding

stem: A capture configured with two SPAN sources, a host access port and the switch uplink, shows every frame from that host twice. Why?
explanation: Each SPAN source observes the same frame at a different point along its path, once entering the access port and once leaving the uplink. The analyser receives both copies because the switch does not de-duplicate across sources in a session.

choices.text: The same frame is observed at two separate points along its path
The analyser NIC receives both the tagged and untagged copy
SPAN retransmits each frame until it is acknowledged
The uplink mirrors both ingress and egress of every frame

stem: Two switches are joined by an 802.1Q trunk. One side uses native VLAN 1 and the other native VLAN 99. What is the immediate consequence?
explanation: 802.1Q does not tag frames belonging to the native VLAN, so each switch delivers them into whatever it considers native. The result is that VLAN 1 and VLAN 99 become one broadcast domain across the link, and CDP reports a native VLAN mismatch.

choices.text: The trunk fails to come up
Untagged frames land in mismatched VLANs, merging two broadcast domains
All tagged frames are dropped
DTP disables the link

stem: A 24-port access switch has a total PoE budget of 370 W. Sixteen ports already deliver 15.4 W each to 802.3af phones. What happens when a seventeenth phone is plugged in?
explanation: Sixteen ports at 15.4 W consume about 246 W, so roughly 124 W remain. The switch's power manager admits the seventeenth device only if its class fits the remaining budget, and refuses power on ports once the budget is exhausted - the link may come up while the phone never boots.

choices.text: Nothing changes, every port can always deliver full power

The switch reboots to rebalance the budget
All ports drop to 7 W to make room

stem: Three switches advertise bridge priorities of 32768, 32768 and 28672 and all have different MAC addresses. Which switch becomes the root bridge?
explanation: Root election compares bridge IDs, and a bridge ID is priority followed by MAC address. Because 28672 is lower than 32768, that switch wins outright and the MAC addresses never enter the comparison.

choices.text: The one with the lowest MAC address among the two at 32768
The switch advertising priority 28672
The oldest switch in the topology
The switch with the highest bridge ID

stem: Rapid PVST+ converges faster than classic 802.1D primarily because of which mechanism?
explanation: RSTP adds the proposal and agreement handshake plus edge-port roles, allowing a new link to move to forwarding in a few hundred milliseconds instead of waiting out the listening and learning timers. Default hello and forward-delay values are unchanged.

choices.text: Shorter hello timers
The proposal and agreement handshake
Disabling STP on edge ports
Using BPDU guard

stem: One side of an EtherChannel is configured as LACP active and the other as LACP passive. What is the outcome?
explanation: LACP active initiates negotiation and passive responds, so the pair forms a bundle. Two passive ports never form because neither speaks first, and an unconditional on port fails to bundle with an LACP port because on does not run the protocol.

choices.text: No bundle, because both sides must be active
A working bundle, because active can initiate with passive
A bundle negotiated with PAgP
The ports are placed in err-disabled state

stem: A port is configured with port-security aging and the aging type set to inactivity. What does that do?
explanation: Inactivity aging removes a secure MAC address when it has not been seen for the configured aging time, freeing the slot for a different device. The default absolute type instead removes every secure address once the timer expires regardless of traffic, which can lock out an active host.

choices.text: It clears the whole table at every reload
It removes a secure address that has been silent for the aging time
It disables port security after the first violation
It converts secure addresses to sticky entries

stem: The MAC address table maps host X to Gi0/5 inside VLAN 20. A frame destined to host X arrives on Gi0/9 inside VLAN 10. How does the switch handle it?
explanation: Table entries are scoped per VLAN, so the lookup in VLAN 10 misses even though a matching address exists for VLAN 20. The switch therefore treats the frame as unknown unicast and floods it only inside VLAN 10, which keeps the two broadcast domains separate.

choices.text: It forwards the frame out Gi0/5
It floods the frame inside VLAN 10 only
It floods the frame in both VLANs
It drops the frame as a MAC move

stem: A blocked port receives an inferior BPDU after a failure somewhere upstream. Which feature lets the switch release that port immediately instead of waiting out the maximum age timer?
explanation: Classic STP cannot tell from a single inferior BPDU whether the topology really changed, so it waits 20 seconds for max age to expire. BackboneFast probes the neighbour for an alternate path to the root bridge and, when one exists, ages the blocked port out at once. UplinkFast only speeds up failover on the switch that loses its own uplink, and Loop Guard prevents a blocked port from being unblocked at all.

choices.text: UplinkFast
BackboneFast
Loop Guard
BPDU Filter

stem: A switch port is cabled to a PC with a straight-through cable, yet the link comes up and passes traffic. What feature explains this?
explanation: Auto-MDIX senses which pin pairs are transmitting and which are receiving, then swaps them inside the port, so a straight-through or crossover cable both work. It depends on the port's speed and duplex being set to auto; hard-coding either one disables the detection and the wrong cable type leaves the link down.

choices.text: The switch always accepts a straight-through cable on access ports and reserves crossover cables for trunks
Auto-MDIX detects the transmit and receive pin pairs and swaps them inside the port
Spanning tree reconfigures the port into a crossover mode when the link fails to come up
The PC's network card inverts its pinout automatically, so only the host side matters

stem: A Layer 2 switch relays a frame from one access port to another. Which header fields does it rewrite?
explanation: Neither MAC address changes and the TTL is not decremented, because a transparent bridge does not participate in the routed path. The frame is forwarded with the original source and destination addresses, which is why a capture taken on the far side of a switch shows the sender's real hardware address rather than the switch's.

choices.text: Both the source and destination MAC addresses
The destination MAC address only
